So I just did the math. If I put in 10% of my pay (75k / year), add in my match (4%), return at a rate of 7% ... I'll have $750,000 in 30 years. I mean, that sounds like a lot, three quarters of a million bucks, but it just really isnt in my world. That's a decent house and property taxes for a couple years. Not only that but the purchasing power of the dollar is dropping like a rock, and I dont know how they adjust for something like that in long term investments. Legitimate question - why should I go for a 401k instead of taking that same money and trying to generate a couple revenue streams? Investment properties or some sort of small business, maybe? I know it's higher risk, but the reward that a basically non-matching 401k offers doesn't really seem to be worth it.

Generally speaking, the answer to that is, to a degree, safety. Yes there are potentially higher rewards to using that money elsewhere, but there's also a higher risk of losing everything. If you posed this question to a personal finance sub I'm sure you could get both detailed reasons why and better advice than I can give you, but the point is not to just make that money grow, its to maximize the return in a way that's also reliable enough that you can count on growth and interest. The idea being that you're not going and getting out all the money and doing something with it: you want it to grow until it replaces part or all of the salary you got by working, just from the interest it generates. This article: http://www.fool.com/teens/teens01.htm is a bit general, and obviously diversification is better than dumping all your money in a 401k, but the fact that your employer will basically give you free extra money to invest in it is nothing to wink at. You say you worry about banking and long term investments, but you also say 750 k isn't a lot in your world. What will your world be 30 years from now? Will you be where you are or doing what you're doing? Its basically all speculation.

Now if, for example, you only put 4% of your salary in that 401k, and they put in 4%, you're effectively getting your investment doubled for free, which is close to 10%, yet you've got another 6% of your pay to invest elsewhere or do other stuff with. There are all kinds of possibilities, and in all honesty you're better off trying to invest now or find other reliable (no, bitcoin or starting your own business don't exactly count, just for the record) ways to build now vs count on earnings later that you have no way of knowing you'll get for certain. Again, people who are already balls deep in this stuff will get you better advice, I just think you're being short-sighted.
